questions.stem: On six trivial instances solver X takes 0.02 s and solver Y 0.2 s; on four hard ones both take 600 s. The plain geometric mean makes Y about four times slower. What happens to the ratio with a shift of 10 s?

options.text: It stays about four, since a shift moves both means by the same amount
options.says: The shift is added before the logarithms, so it changes the ratio: the lesson's C and D go from 3.162 to 1.006.

options.text: It becomes exactly one, since every value is floored at one inside the logarithm
options.says: The floor only lifts v + s below 1; with s = 10 nothing is floored, and the lesson's similar case gives 1.006, not 1.

options.text: It falls close to one, since differences far below the shift barely count
options.says: Right: with s = 10 the fractions of a second vanish against the shift, and the tied hard instances dominate.

options.text: It flips below one, since the shift always favours the solver slower on easy instances
options.says: The shift does not favour either solver; X and Y tie on the hard instances, so nothing can put Y ahead.

origin.section: The Shifted Geometric Mean Summarizes Ratios, and Its Shift Keeps Easy Instances From Dominating

questions.stem: A teammate times HiGHS and SCIP 'to optimality' through MathOpt with no gap target set. Both report OPTIMAL on every instance. What is wrong with comparing the two timings?

options.text: The two stop at different gaps, since each uses its own default target
options.says: Right: HiGHS's mip_rel_gap defaults to 1e-4 and SCIP's limits/gap to 0; the lesson's HiGHS stopped with its bound $5k above its plan.

options.text: Nothing is wrong, since OPTIMAL means a gap of zero for every solver
options.says: HiGHS reported OPTIMAL with a gap of 0.0089% in the lesson's run: OPTIMAL means within the solver's own target.

options.text: The two report OPTIMAL too early, since MathOpt overrides both default targets
options.says: MathOpt leaves each solver's default when no target is set; that is exactly why the two differ.

options.text: Nothing is wrong, since both solvers divide their gap by the same value
options.says: They do not: HiGHS divides by its primal bound, SCIP by the smaller of the two values.

origin.section: Fix the Gap Target Before You Time Anything, Then Measure Time-to-Gap

questions.stem: Switching a setting cut one instance's LP iterations by 25% with seed 1. The team wants to adopt it. What should it run before deciding?

options.text: The same instance and seed again, so a second run can confirm the saving
options.says: A deterministic count repeats exactly on the same instance and seed, so a rerun adds no evidence.

options.text: The same instance with more threads, so the saving is checked under load
options.says: More threads make the path less repeatable and answer a different question; the lesson compares on one thread.

options.text: The same instance timed by the clock, so the saving is shown in seconds
options.says: Wall time adds noise to a within-solver comparison that a deterministic count already makes exactly.

options.text: Every instance with every seed, both ways, so each pair is an observation
options.says: Right: the lesson's presolve switch saved 32% on one pair yet scored 0.996 over all 18 pairs.

origin.section: Compare Settings of One Solver Pairwise, Over Every Seed
